answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost.
